Spot mutants killed by these tests: rope style ignored, rope_attn_factor ignored, attn_scale without YaRN mscale, norm_topk_prob ignored, OLMoE full-width qk_norm skipped.

hypotheses_validated.claim: With emulate_act_quant the reference applies F32/F16/BF16/Q8/Q4 matrices bit-identically to the engine kernels (NUMERICS 2-3) on scalar, AVX2 and AVX-512.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_matvec_bit_identical_to_engine_kernels against a kernels-only DLL built from T02's engine/src/quant.c + quant_avx2.c + quant_avx512.c (state at 09:33): uint32 bit patterns equal for all 5 dtypes, 3 ISAs, incl. zero blocks, tiny/large magnitudes and exact .5 rounding ties; a half-away-from-zero act-quant mutant is killed.

hypotheses_validated.claim: numpy F16 and BF16 encoders are bit-identical to the native converter (RNE, overflow to inf, quiet NaN with truncated payload).
hypotheses_validated.evidence: 1.1M random float32 bit patterns + 100k normals compared against hearth_quantize(F16/BF16): 0 mismatches after aligning NaN payload handling with vcvtps2ph.

hypotheses_validated.claim: make_tiny routing margins are far above float-order noise, so engine/reference routing equality (INV-NUM-2) does not hinge on near-ties.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Replacing the canonical dot16/sum16 with numpy's own float32 order changes router selection scores by <= 7.2e-7 and logits by <= 6e-6 on all golden-style models; make_tiny enforces >= 3e-4 absolute (sigmoid), >= 2e-3 relative (softmax) and >= 6e-4 group-score gaps on the golden token sequence, redrawing the offending router (at most 1 redraw observed for the 11 golden models).

hypotheses_validated.claim: The container reader rejects malformed files with ValueError (never IndexError/struct.error/crash).
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_malformed_files_raise: 29 corruptions (empty, short, magic, version, align, truncations, out-of-range/huge section offsets and counts, tensor offset/alignment/nbytes/dtype/ndim/shape/name, slab alignment/range/size/dtype/missing, metadata overrun and unknown type) all raise ValueError.

hypotheses_validated.claim: FP8 e4m3 block-scaled checkpoints (DeepSeek/Kimi style, weight_scale_inv) convert to the same model as their dequantized weights, through both the safe_open+torch reader and the numpy fallback reader.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_fp8_checkpoint_end_to_end[torch|numpy]: synthetic FP8 DeepSeek-V3 checkpoint (32x32 blocks, partial edge blocks) converted to F32 matches transformers run on the dequantized weights within 2e-3; e4m3 table equals torch's float8_e4m3fn decode for all 256 codes; backends agree bit-for-bit on a bf16 checkpoint incl. row slices.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Reference evaluation is order-independent: eval(batch) == sequence of eval([t]), KV cache persists across calls, reset() clears it; power-of-two emb/residual scales are exactly invisible with eps=0, logit_scale is exact, tied == untied-with-copied-head.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_kv_cache_across_calls_and_reset (5 archs), test_scales_and_tied_embeddings (bit-exact comparisons; residual/emb/logit/tie mutants killed).

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Activation-quantization emulation keeps quantized-model logits within 5% of exact-weight float evaluation token by token.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: On Q8 tiny models act-quant noise occasionally flips a routing decision, producing a single-token logit difference up to 0.32 x max|logit|; median per-token error stays ~1.5%. The test now bounds the median. This is why golden Q4 tests must compare the engine with the emulating reference.
